problem: Building simulatable, realistic 3D scenes for embodied AI depends on artist-designed assets. Prior real-to-sim conversions (Scan2CAD, R3DS, ACDC) use limited-diversity CAD libraries and record no rationale for choosing one candidate over another, so automated replica creation lacks a principled recipe.
motivation: Embodied agents need scalable, diverse, realistic and interactable scenes, including small items, for skill learning and sim-to-real transfer. Real scans contain this diversity but cannot be simulated directly. Human rankings over many candidate assets per object can supervise a learned asset-selection model, removing the need for artists.
key_idea: Build a large real-scan-to-simulation dataset in which each scanned object has about 10 candidate assets (generated or retrieved), human-ranked and placed. Then train a multi-modal (image+text to point cloud) alignment model on those rankings to automate asset replacement.
insight: Training on the human-preference ranking annotations matters: the same ULIP-2 alignment pretrained on Objaverse reaches only 13.1% Top-1 with I+T→P, versus 28.4% for the trained model. Point-cloud-based pose alignment is more robust than ACDC's render-and-compare under occlusion (ScanNet++ IoU 0.40 vs 0.24). Navigation policies trained on the real-scan-derived scenes generalize better to held-out real domains than ones trained on procedural ProcTHOR scenes (SR 50.67 vs 45.33), suggesting realism of layouts and objects matters.
method: Room layout estimation: a pretrained layout transformer predicts floor plan, walls and ceiling from the point cloud, with a heuristic max-contour-area floor plan as backup.

Object asset curation: SAM masks the clearest view of each object, GPT-4V captions it, and 10 candidates are collected via text-to-3D (Shape-E), image-to-3D (TripoSR, InstantMesh, Michelangelo) and text-to-3D retrieval from Objaverse (Uni3D, ULIP), with Paint3D texture optimization.

Human annotation: annotators pick the best asset, adjust its pose/scale in the scene, and rank the other candidates (top 2-5 as acceptable), enabling top-5 augmentation; 10% batch QC with 98% pass threshold.

Physics-based optimization: a scene graph (SceneVerse-style, 96.3% relation accuracy on 10 scenes) plus MCMC sampling minimizing pairwise bbox-IoU collisions; Blender import with GPT-derived mass, friction and bounciness.

Optimal asset retrieval model: frozen ULIP-2 image/text encoders, a learnable point-cloud encoder (Point-BERT), and an MLP head on point features; a softmax loss over summed image/text/point scores (L_match) plus an auxiliary cross-scene candidate loss (L_aux).
Object pose alignment: heuristic centre translation, longest-side bbox scaling, and yaw search in 30° steps to best match the scanned bbox.
Micro-scene synthesis task: 1,012 micro-scenes (a large furniture item plus small objects on it), benchmarked with ATISS, DiffuScene and PhyScene.

setting.backbone: Retrieval model: ULIP-2 frozen image/text encoders (OpenCLIP) + fine-tuned Point-BERT 3D encoder; navigation agent: SPOC (SigLIP encoders, 3-layer transformer encoder/decoder) trained with imitation learning
setting.training_data: Retrieval model: 600 scenes / 13,125 objects from MetaScenes annotations. Navigation: 100 shortest-path trajectories per training scene from MetaScenes (706 scenes, 4:1 train/test split), or ProcTHOR, or both; 70k steps, batch size 256.
setting.observation: Navigation agent: egocentric RGB with SigLIP encoders and a 10-step context window; the replica-creation model uses object images, text and point clouds from ScanNet scans.
setting.action_space: Low-level: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°
setting.simulator: AI Habitat (navigation); Blender for scene assembly
setting.privileged: Scene replicas are built from scans with human annotations. Navigation demonstrations use the simulator's shortest-path planner (PathFinder) and object semantics. Test-time agent uses none beyond the object-goal target.

results: The trained retrieval model reaches Top-1 28.4% and Top-5 76.0%, versus the best baseline Top-1 of 16.5% (GPT-4V) and Top-5 of 66.6% (CLIP). Pose alignment beats ACDC. SPOC trained on MetaScenes beats ProcTHOR-trained SPOC on held-out real scenes (SR 52.64 vs 51.21) and held-out ScanNet++ domain (50.67 vs 45.33), and beats HSSD-trained SPOC on ReplicaCAD (32 vs 27).
limitations: The retrieval model reaches only 28.4% Top-1, so fully automated replication is still far from human choices.
The navigation evaluation is small and non-standard (single SPOC baseline, 10 held-out ScanNet++ scenes, 100 ReplicaCAD trajectories), and combining data sources did not consistently help.
Pose alignment is heuristic (bbox-based, 30° yaw steps), and physical properties come from GPT prompts rather than measurement.
